name: Your claim is to the work, not its results
meaning: Put your full effort into what is yours to do, and loosen your grip on how it turns out; outcomes depend on many factors you do not control.
applies_when: Anxiety about outcomes (exams, interviews, launches, results you are waiting for) is paralysing or distorting the work itself.
misleads_when: It is used to ignore consequences, skip planning, excuse harm to others ('I did my part'), or to justify unfair pay or treatment by someone with power over you.
modern_application: List what is in your control this week (preparation, effort, honesty) and what is not (the examiner, the market, other people). Judge yourself only on the first list.

name: Stay the same in success and failure
meaning: Evenness of mind when things go well or badly is itself the discipline; success and failure both pass.
applies_when: A result (good or bad) is swinging your mood and self-worth, or you are about to make a big decision on the high or low of one outcome.
misleads_when: It is used to suppress real disappointment or joy, or to stop learning from what went wrong.
modern_application: Before reacting to a result, wait a day, then ask: what would I do next if this had gone the other way? Usually the next step is the same.

name: Yoga is skill in action
meaning: Doing your work with full attention and steadiness, without being distracted by attachment, is itself a spiritual practice.
applies_when: Work feels separate from what matters to you, or you want your everyday job to be meaningful.
misleads_when: It turns into perfectionism, or into the idea that only flawless work counts.
modern_application: Pick one task today and give it unbroken attention for 25 minutes, phone away. Notice the quality of attention, not the output.

name: Act rather than withdraw
meaning: No one can avoid acting altogether; doing what is yours to do is better than inaction, and stepping back does not by itself bring freedom.
applies_when: Someone is tempted to avoid a responsibility by doing nothing, or hopes that withdrawing will make a problem disappear.
misleads_when: The person genuinely needs rest, is burnt out or ill, or is in danger; then pausing or leaving is right, and moderation applies.
modern_application: Name the one action you have been avoiding and do the smallest first step of it today.

name: No sincere effort is wasted
meaning: Effort towards the good is never lost, even when it falls short; a person who tries and slips comes to no ruin and can start again from where they were.
applies_when: Someone has failed, relapsed or fallen short and believes all their effort was for nothing.
misleads_when: It is used to keep pouring effort into a path that is clearly wrong for the person (sunk cost).
modern_application: Write down three things your effort built that remain even though the result failed (skills, habits, relationships). Restart from those, not from zero.

name: Your own path, imperfect, over someone else's
meaning: Living out your own duty and nature, even imperfectly, is better than performing someone else's role well.
applies_when: Someone is copying a path (career, lifestyle) because it looks impressive on others, against their own nature and responsibilities.
misleads_when: It is used to keep people in roles assigned by caste, gender or family against their will. Traditionally the verse spoke of social duty; Viveka never uses it to confine anyone.
modern_application: Write two lists: what draws you to the other path, and what in your own situation only you can do. Choose from the second list.

name: Do everything as an offering
meaning: Whatever you do, eat, give or endure can be done as an offering, which frees the act from selfish grasping.
applies_when: Daily work feels empty or self-centred, or someone wants a simple way to bring meaning into ordinary tasks.
misleads_when: It is used to make someone accept exploitation as 'service'.
modern_application: Before one routine task each day, dedicate it silently to someone or something larger than yourself.

name: Others follow what you do
meaning: Whatever a respected person does, others copy; those who lead should act well and help others without unsettling them.
applies_when: Parents, teachers, managers or older siblings are deciding how to behave, knowing others watch them.
misleads_when: It turns into performing virtue for an audience rather than acting from conviction.
modern_application: Ask: if the people who look up to me copied exactly what I am about to do, would I be glad?

name: Act for the welfare of all
meaning: Act so as to hold the world together, delighting in the welfare of all beings, not only your own gain.
applies_when: Choosing between a narrow personal gain and something that serves the wider community.
misleads_when: It is used to demand self-sacrifice from people who are already over-giving or neglecting their own basic needs.
modern_application: Add one question to your decision: who else is affected, and how does this option leave them?

name: Give up the fruit, not the work
meaning: True relinquishment means giving up attachment to results while still doing your duties; no embodied person can give up action entirely.
applies_when: Someone thinks spiritual seriousness means dropping their responsibilities.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss a person's real need to step away from something harmful.
modern_application: Keep the commitment; change the attitude. Write down the specific result you are clinging to, and decide to do the work well whatever it brings.

name: Don't drop a duty only because it is hard
meaning: Giving up what you should do just because it is painful or tiring is a lesser kind of letting go and brings no real freedom.
applies_when: Someone wants to quit a course, job or commitment mainly because it has become difficult or uncomfortable.
misleads_when: The difficulty is abuse, danger, exploitation or harm to health. Then leaving is right, and Viveka always supports it.
modern_application: Separate 'hard' from 'harmful': list what makes it hard (effort, boredom, fear) and what, if anything, makes it harmful. Only the second list is a reason to leave.

name: Give back what sustains you
meaning: Life runs on mutual nourishment; taking benefits without giving anything back is called theft.
applies_when: Someone is taking more than they give in a family, team or community, or feels unappreciated for what they give.
misleads_when: It is used to keep score in close relationships, or to pressure someone into repaying help they never asked for.
modern_application: List who sustains your daily life. Choose one way to give back to one of them this week.

name: Give because it is right to give
meaning: The best gift is given because giving is right, at the right time and place, to someone who cannot repay it; gifts given for a return, grudgingly or with contempt are lesser.
applies_when: Deciding whether, how or to whom to give money, time or help.
misleads_when: It pushes someone to give beyond their means, or to tolerate being taken advantage of.
modern_application: Before giving, check three things: am I expecting something back, is this the right moment, and will it actually help?

name: Weigh consequences, harm and your own capacity
meaning: Action begun without regard for its consequences, the loss it causes, harm to others or one's own capacity comes from delusion.
applies_when: An impulsive or dramatic decision is being made without thinking through its effects.
misleads_when: It becomes endless deliberation that prevents any action.
modern_application: Before acting, write four lines: likely consequences, what it could cost, who could be hurt, and whether you can actually carry it through.

name: Understand what action really is
meaning: Even the wise are confused about action and inaction; one must understand what right action, wrong action and non-action are before acting.
applies_when: A situation is morally confusing, and doing nothing might itself be a harmful choice.
misleads_when: It is used to excuse never deciding.
modern_application: Ask: what happens if I do nothing? Treat that as an option with consequences, not as a neutral default.

name: Moderation in eating, sleep, work and rest
meaning: Discipline is not for those who overdo or underdo eating, sleep or effort; balance in daily life is what ends sorrow.
applies_when: Burnout, sleeplessness, overwork, crash diets, or extreme routines in the name of discipline.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss a real emergency that needs intense effort for a short time.
modern_application: Check four dials this week: sleep, food, work hours and rest. Adjust the one furthest from moderate.

name: Practice and detachment train the mind
meaning: The mind is restless, but it can be steadied by repeated practice and by letting go; when it wanders, bring it back.
applies_when: Someone feels their mind or habits are impossible to change, or keeps losing focus.
misleads_when: It is used to blame someone with a medical or mental-health condition for not 'trying hard enough'.
modern_application: Choose one small daily practice (ten minutes of focus, a walk, a journal) and track only whether you returned to it, not how well it went.

name: Don't work for show
meaning: Action or discipline done to gain respect, honour or display is unstable and fleeting.
applies_when: Effort is being shaped mainly by how it will look to others: likes, status or praise.
misleads_when: It makes someone ashamed of wanting fair recognition for their work.
modern_application: Do one good thing this week that no one will know about.

name: Keep acting even when you have nothing to gain
meaning: Even one who needs nothing keeps acting, because others follow and the world is held together by such action.
applies_when: After retirement, success or financial security, someone wonders why they should keep contributing.
misleads_when: It denies people well-earned rest, or pressures elders who have little energy left.
modern_application: Offer one regular, modest contribution (mentoring, teaching, volunteering) that uses what you already know.

name: Discipline is not self-torture
meaning: Harsh austerities that torment the body, done from obstinacy or ego, or to harm another, are condemned; discipline should serve life.
applies_when: Extreme fasting, punishing routines, self-harm framed as discipline, or 'proving' oneself through suffering.
misleads_when: It is used to avoid any discomfort at all.
modern_application: If a practice is hurting your body or health, stop it and speak to someone you trust or a professional. Discipline that harms you is not what this teaching asks.
